thread.title: Dow Jones Cools As Apple Stays On Track To $1.25 Trillion Market Cap

author: DAVID SAITO-CHUNG
title: Dow Jones Cools As Apple Stays On Track To $1.25 Trillion Market Cap
text:
U.S. stocks today showed mixed action as investors shrugged off concern over the conviction of President Trump's former campaign manager and the admission by a key Trump lawyer to committing fraud. Oil stocks rallied. Apple snapped a light two-session selling streak.
X The Nasdaq composite rose 0.4% while the S&P 500 was virtually flat. The Dow Jones industrial average fell less than 0.2%.
U.S. crude oil futures jumped more than 3% to $67.89 a barrel.
Small caps rose marginally, with the Russell 2000 gaining 0.1%.
United Technologies ( UTX ) and Boeing ( BA ) led the downside among the 30 components, each falling more than 2 points. United Tech and Boeing are currently forming new bases .
United Tech, a giant in aircraft engines and Otis elevators, has formed a four-week handle on its six-month cup base. The new buy point is 136.76, 10 cents above the handle's high.
Notice on a daily chart how United Tech had tried to form a base after peaking at 139.24 on Jan. 29. The stock quickly corrected 12.3% in price to a near-term low of 122.21, then quickly rebounded. However, United Tech failed to break out. Rather, it needed more time to form the left side of a new base.
Please read this Investor's Corner on the key base patterns that form among the true stock market leaders and the minimum amount of time required to build each chart pattern.
Fellow Dow Jones industrial member Apple ( AAPL ) inched higher to 215.29, reaffirming that the balance of supply vs. demand for its shares is clearly tilted to the latter.
Apple now holds a 27% gain year to date, vs. a less than 7% lift by the S&P 500.
The iPhone giant broke out of a base on base at 194.30 four weeks ago and is now extended.
Once a stock has broken out, the ideal time to buy is when shares remain within the 5% buy zone . In Apple's case, the 5% buy zone went from 194.30 to 204.02.
(Please read this Stock Market Today column on reasons why Apple is off to a good start toward reaping further gains after recently eclipsing the $1 trillion market cap barrier.)
Retail Stock Breaks Out, Reverses Urban Outfitters ( URBN ) spiked up at the open, rising as much as 10% to a session high of 52.50. But shares barreled lower to a 2% loss. The trendy fashion apparel and interior goods retailer smashed Wall Street's consensus forecast with earnings jumping 91% to 84 cents a share on a 14% pickup in revenue to $993 million.
Urban had grown profit by 2%, 21% and 280% in the prior three quarters on top-line gains of 4%, 6% and 12%.
The stock is now mildly below a 48.34 prime buy point in an eight-week flat base .
Urban tried to break out past that entry point on Aug. 10 but did not get far. Ultimately, the stock continued work on the key chart pattern for hot growth stocks.
An alternate buy point at 49.10, 10 cents above new high of 49 within the base, provided a different entry.
IPO Stocks Setting Up Roku ( ROKU ), a Sept. 28, 2017, new issue at $14 a share, rallied more than 1% to 59.36. The stock gapped up bullishly on Aug. 9 after posting much better than expected quarterly results. Roku has been hitting strong upside resistance near 59-60.
The video streaming hardware firm reported a profit of a penny a share as revenue grew 57% to $156.8 million, the second most for any given quarter.
Revenue growth has now accelerated for a second quarter in a row, following increases of 27% in Q4 2017 and 36% in Q1 of this year.
Other IPO stocks doing well this week:
Tilray ( TLRY ), down 2%: The British Columbia-based developer and supplier of cannabis medicines and extracts cleared a four-week IPO base at 34.20 on Monday. The company posted a net loss of 9 cents a share in 2017 as revenue rose 62% to $21 million. Average dollar volume is fierce at more than $50 million per day over the past few weeks.
Goosehead Insurance ( GSHD ), up fractionally: The Westlake, Texas-based specialist in property and casualty insurance recently bounced nicely off its 50-day moving average, offering a follow-on entry point near 25. After peaking at 29.73 on July 19, shares may be forming a new base .
